messages:
marta: Quick thought — we need to settle on approach for long-term refactor of request-routing + policy layer. Two options on the table:
marta: (A) Consolidate into a single service that owns routing, policy, and some lighter transform logic.
marta: (B) Keep small per-surface services and add a thin facade/gateway that composes them.

devon: main trade I see: consolidation reduces cross-service RPCs and simplifies data ownership, but risks larger blast radius and slower deploy cycles.

raj: +1 on consolidation for perf reasons. Our p95 suffers with the current fan-out for multi-model requests.
raj: but we need clear contract boundaries if we go big. Otherwise we just move tech debt inside one monolith.

olivia: facade gives teams autonomy (can iterate their own adapters) and keeps deploy size small. But adds latency and brittle orchestration.

marta: exactly — both sides have pros. I'm leaning to a hybrid: consolidate core routing + KV-cache ownership into a single "routing-core" microservice, keep model-adapters as separate small services behind well-defined APIs.

devon: that seems sensible. Routing-core would manage request lifecycle, KV cache, batching decisions and fallback policies. adapters only translate to model runtimes.

raj: if we do that we should codify the adapter interface now. Proto or OpenAPI? I vote protobuf for binary + streaming.

olivia: agree on proto for runtime calls. For admin/console endpoints OpenAPI is nicer.

marta: draft interface sketch:

```
service Adapter {
  rpc Predict(stream PredictRequest) returns (stream PredictResponse);
  rpc Health(HealthCheck) returns (HealthStatus);
}

message PredictRequest { string req_id = 1; bytes prompt = 2; map<string,string> meta = 3; }
```

raj: looks good. Also need a thin compatibility shim for older adapters during migration.

devon: migration plan ideas:
- build routing-core behind feature flag in prod
- mirror traffic (shadow) for 2 weeks, compare p95/p99 and error rates
- enable canary for a small percentage with fallback to old router
- roll forward once metrics stable

marta: add operational requirements: SLOs for adapter calls, clear timeout semantics, circuit-breakers, and tracing so we can attribute latency.

olivia: also add automated contract tests in CI: mocked routing-core <-> adapter tests + integration test that runs a small local model.

raj: spike action: I'll prototype routing-core + one adapter shim (2 weeks). Will measure latency on batch sizes we care about.

marta: devon, can you scope infra needs? particularly KV cache placement and whether it lives inside routing-core or as an external redis/rocks service.

devon: initial thought: routing-core should own an in-memory hot KV cache (local LRU) + fallback to shared redis for cold keys. Keeps hot path fast and allows horizontal scaling.

marta: good. security note: adapters must authenticate via mTLS and project-scoped tokens. Add to RFC.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline for routing-core created: pipelines/routing-core/ci/ — initial lint + unit tests passing on main.

olivia: can we include a migration checklist in the RFC? e.g., metrics to compare, rollback criteria, client-library bump plan.

marta: yes. draft RFC items so far: rationale, interface spec, infra topology, migration plan, testing matrix, security controls, SLOs, rollout steps.

devon: ACK. I'll start a repo skeleton and a pages RFC template today.

raj: tagging timeline: spike 2w, RFC 1w to iterate, 4w for initial canary, then iterate. total ~8–10w to first stable rollout.

marta: sounds realistic. final ask: please add any missing failure modes (e.g., cache poisoning, adapter misbehavior) to the RFC risk section.

olivia: I'll add runbook sections for degradations and fallback to legacy router.

marta: thanks — assigning ownership: marta = RFC owner, devon = infra, raj = spike lead, olivia = ops/runbooks.

marta: next step: I'll create the RFC draft and link it here by EOD.

deploy-bot: rfc/routing-core-draft created at https://gitlab.redwood/rfcs/334 — CI link: https://ci.redwood/pipelines/8912

devon: reviewing now, will comment on infra bits in the RFC thread.

raj: starting spike branch: spike/routing-core-proto

olivia: will start a draft of contract tests and a checklist in the RFC doc.

marta: great, thanks everyone. We'll sync in the architecture meeting on Thursday for signoff.
